preamble: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  ACC/AHA 2020 HCM Guidelines / ESC 2014 HCM Guidelines / HCM Risk-SCD Model  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is maximum LV wall thickness ≥30 mm on echo or CMR?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — massive hypertrophy; major SCD risk factor; strongly supports ICD implantation per ACC/AHA

questions.question: Does CMR show late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving >15% of LV mass?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — extensive fibrosis confirmed; >15% LGE is a major independent SCD risk factor; ICD implantation recommended

questions.question: Is there documented non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT ≥3 beats, ≥120 bpm) on Holter or event monitor?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — NSVT confirmed; major SCD risk factor in HCM Risk-SCD calculator; prompts ICD discussion

questions.question: Is there an abnormal blood pressure response to exercise (failure to rise ≥20 mmHg or a drop) on stress test?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — inability to augment cardiac output; predicts SCD particularly in patients <40 years

questions.question: Is the resting LVOT gradient ≥50 mmHg on Doppler echo (severe obstruction)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe resting obstruction; symptomatic HOCM; septal reduction therapy (myectomy or alcohol ablation) indicated per ACC/AHA Class I

questions.question: Does LVOT gradient rise to ≥50 mmHg with Valsalva or exercise provocation?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — labile obstruction confirmed; physiologic stress unmasks severe gradient; equivalent to resting obstruction for intervention eligibility

questions.question: Is LVEF <50% on echo or CMR (HCM burned-out phase with systolic dysfunction)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — end-stage/burned-out HCM with systolic dysfunction; worst prognosis subgroup; heart failure hospitalization and transplant listing risk elevated

questions.question: Is LV end-diastolic diameter >54 mm (men) / >50 mm (women) on echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — LV dilation in HCM indicates transition to dilated phase; associated with progressive heart failure and higher mortality

questions.question: Is there Grade III diastolic dysfunction (restrictive filling: E/A >2, deceleration time <150 ms, E/e' >14)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — restrictive diastolic pattern; elevated LA pressures; high heart failure hospitalization risk

questions.question: Is there documented paroxysmal, persistent, or permanent atrial fibrillation on ECG or monitor?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — AF present in ~20–25% of HCM; major cause of heart failure progression and stroke; anticoagulation mandatory; rhythm control challenging

questions.question: Is LA diameter >45 mm or LA volume index >34 mL/m² on echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe LA dilation; strong predictor of AF development and stroke risk in HCM; associated with worse symptom burden and outcomes

questions.question: Is there a pathogenic variant in MYH7 or TNNT2 (associated with early-onset severe phenotype and high SCD risk)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high-risk sarcomere variant confirmed; MYH7 and TNNT2 variants associated with more severe hypertrophy, earlier onset, and higher SCD rates than MYBPC3

questions.question: Is there sudden cardiac death in a first- or second-degree relative under age 50?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — family SCD history; independent risk factor in HCM Risk-SCD calculator; lowers ICD threshold

questions.question: Is the patient NYHA Class III or IV despite optimal medical therapy (beta-blocker, verapamil, disopyramide)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — refractory symptoms on maximal medical therapy; septal reduction therapy or advanced heart failure management indicated

questions.question: Is there a history of unexplained syncope or near-syncope during or immediately after exertion?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — exercise-induced syncope in HCM; high SCD risk marker; ICD implantation strongly considered
